plain_english_title: Safety Checklist Before Challenging an Old Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) Decision for CUE
what_this_means: Challenging an older final Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision for Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) carries a high-stakes procedural rule that surprises many Veterans: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue—even if an attorney later spots a much stronger legal error in the exact same Board decision. This checklist explains the five safety checks an accredited representative performs before ever filing a Board CUE motion.
record_clues: A prior final Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision in your C-file that decided the specific disability rating or service-connection issue you are questioning.

Any earlier letters or motions in your C-file mentioning 'Clear and Unmistakable Error' or 'motion for revision' (important to check whether one was already decided on the merits or dismissed without prejudice).
Historical VA Rating Code Sheets showing whether correcting the error would have changed your combined monthly compensation percentage on that date.
important_cautions: Single Merits Decision Limit (38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)): Filing a quick, handwritten, or incomplete Board CUE motion that gets denied on the merits permanently closes future Board CUE motions on that Board decision issue (though a dismissal without prejudice for lack of specificity under § 20.1404 does not count as a merits decision).
If a federal court (such as the CAVC) already reviewed and decided that specific issue on the merits, the Board no longer has authority to revise it via CUE.
Arguments that VA failed to get records, provided a poor C&P exam, weighed conflicting medical opinions unfairly, or failed to apply a later change in law are excluded from CUE by regulation.
questions_for_representative: Can we check whether newly located service department records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) can reopen this issue at the Regional Office (RO) without risking my one merits Board CUE opportunity?
Has any prior Board CUE motion ever been decided on the merits for this issue in my C-file, or was this Board issue ever decided on appeal by the CAVC?
Have we pulled the exact word-for-word 38 C.F.R. regulation in effect on the date of the Board decision and verified that the Combined Ratings Table math would have increased my monthly payment?
